skill.name: flow-nexus-platform
skill.description: Manage Flow Nexus accounts, remote sandboxes, deployments, storage, billing, challenges, and monitoring through documented MCP tools.
skill.summary: Operate core Flow Nexus services from one MCP workflow guide.
skill.author: ruvnet

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, JavaScript template strings, and placeholder credentials. Confirmed risks include outbound network access, repository cloning, remote command execution, secret transmission, paid actions, delegated tools, and destructive platform mutations. No prompt injection, obfuscation, or embedded live credential was found.

remediation.issue: Remote code, shell commands, and packages can execute untrusted content.
remediation.suggestion: Require a user-approved command and package plan, pin trusted versions and commits, disable package lifecycle scripts where possible, and enforce sandbox resource limits.

remediation.issue: Examples encourage sending API keys and database credentials to hosted operations.
remediation.suggestion: Use scoped secret references from an approved secret store, redact logs, prevent plaintext prompt entry, and document the external trust boundary.

remediation.issue: Payment links and auto-refill settings can create charges.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation that shows amount, currency, threshold, recurrence, and account before every paid or auto-refill change.

remediation.issue: Publishing, deployment, account changes, and deletions can create irreversible effects.
remediation.suggestion: Add previews, ownership checks, scoped authorization, target identifiers, and separate confirmations for public, destructive, or entitlement-changing operations.

remediation.issue: Delegated assistant tools can create swarms and deploy code.
remediation.suggestion: Default delegated tools to disabled, use a minimal allowlist, constrain budgets and destinations, and require approval for each external action.

semantic_findings.title: Remote Code and Command Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs agents to install packages and execute caller-supplied code and shell commands in remote sandboxes. Malicious inputs or dependencies can execute untrusted code and consume resources.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited examples directly provide run_commands, startup_script, package installation, and sandbox_execute inputs.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Credentials Sent to Hosted Operations
semantic_findings.description: Examples pass API keys, database URLs, application secrets, and an Anthropic key into Flow Nexus operations. Real replacements would disclose credentials to a community-operated external service.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented MCP parameters explicitly accept API keys, database connection strings, secrets, and an Anthropic key.

semantic_findings.title: Financial Actions and Recurring Charges
semantic_findings.description: The skill can create payment links and enable automatic credit purchases. Agent execution without explicit approval could cause unintended charges.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly configure a payment amount and enable auto-refill with a recurring purchase threshold.

semantic_findings.title: Delegated Assistant Can Invoke Tools
semantic_findings.description: The Seraphina example enables tools that can create swarms and deploy code. Delegation can expand impact beyond the user's immediate request.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example sets enable_tools to true and states that the assistant can create swarms and deploy code.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive and Public Platform Mutations
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents sandbox deletion, storage deletion, application publication, application updates, and template deployment. Incorrect targets can destroy data or expose unreviewed source code.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited MCP calls directly delete resources, publish source code, update applications, and deploy templates.

semantic_findings.title: Caller-Supplied Entitlement and Credit Mutations
semantic_findings.description: Examples accept caller-supplied user identifiers, tiers, credit amounts, and reasons for entitlement changes. Weak server authorization could permit balance or tier abuse.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The parameters support direct account and credit mutations, but server-side authorization behavior is not present in the audited file.

content.value_statement: Flow Nexus workflows span many tools and operational domains. This skill provides one guide for accounts, sandboxes, deployments, billing, storage, and monitoring.
actual_capabilities: Register users, authenticate sessions, reset passwords, verify email, and update profiles through Flow Nexus MCP tools.
Create, configure, inspect, stop, and delete remote sandboxes for supported development templates.
Execute code, install packages, run startup commands, upload files, and inspect logs within remote sandboxes.
Search, publish, update, and deploy applications and templates through the Flow Nexus marketplace.
Check balances, create payment links, configure auto-refill, and review transaction history.
Manage challenges, storage objects, real-time subscriptions, execution streams, system health, and audit logs.
limitations: Requires a configured Flow Nexus MCP server and an authenticated Flow Nexus account.
Remote execution, storage, deployment, and marketplace actions depend on current platform permissions and service availability.
The guide provides examples, but it does not validate external packages, repositories, application code, or uploaded data.
Billing, deletion, publication, and account changes can create costs or irreversible effects and require user review.

use_cases.title: Prototype in remote sandboxes
use_cases.description: Create an isolated Node.js or Python environment, install dependencies, run code, and inspect logs before deployment.

use_cases.title: Operate hosted applications
use_cases.description: Search templates, deploy services, publish updates, monitor execution, and manage stored artifacts from one workflow.

use_cases.title: Track usage and learning
use_cases.description: Review balances, transactions, challenges, achievements, and leaderboards while controlling paid credit settings.

prompt_templates.title: Check account and platform status
prompt_templates.prompt: Check my Flow Nexus authentication status, credit balance, active sandboxes, and system health. Summarize results without making changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with a read-only platform overview.

prompt_templates.title: Create a development sandbox
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Node.js sandbox named [name] with [packages]. Do not include secrets. Show the planned configuration before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a basic isolated development environment.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy a reviewed application
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a suitable [category] template, compare options, and prepare deployment [name]. Ask before deploying or adding paid resources.
prompt_templates.scenario: Move a reviewed application toward deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a controlled production workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a staged Flow Nexus workflow for [application]. Include sandbox tests, pinned dependencies, secret handling, deployment approval, monitoring, rollback, and cost controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate advanced production operations with safeguards.

output_examples.input: Check my platform status without changing anything.
output: Sandboxes: two running and one stopped.

output_examples.input: Prepare a Node.js sandbox with Express and dotenv, but ask before creation.
output_examples.output: Prepared a Node.js sandbox plan with two packages, no secrets, a one-hour timeout, and confirmation required before creation.

output_examples.input: Compare backend templates and prepare a deployment plan for inventory-api.
output_examples.output: Compared suitable backend templates and prepared a staged deployment plan with testing, secret references, cost review, monitoring, and rollback.

best_practices: Review and confirm every payment, auto-refill, publication, deployment, deletion, and account change before execution.
Use scoped secrets through approved secret storage, and never place live credentials in prompts, examples, logs, or source code.
Pin trusted packages and repository revisions, test in isolated sandboxes, monitor costs, and remove unused resources promptly.
anti_patterns: Do not enable delegated tools or arbitrary shell commands without an explicit allowlist and user approval.
Do not upload sensitive files to public buckets or return public URLs for confidential data.
Do not assume example prices, limits, tiers, endpoints, or platform behavior remain current.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: You need a configured Flow Nexus MCP server, an authenticated account, and permissions for the requested operations.

faq.question: Can this skill run code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can request code execution in remote sandboxes, so review all code, commands, packages, and resource limits first.

faq.question: Can this skill create charges?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create payment links and configure auto-refill. Paid actions should require explicit confirmation.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use scoped secrets from approved secret storage. Never place live credentials in prompts, examples, logs, or published application source.

faq.question: Can it publish or delete resources?
faq.answer: Yes. It can publish applications and delete sandboxes or files. Confirm ownership, target identifiers, visibility, and recovery options.

faq.question: Does it verify third-party code?
faq.answer: No. Review and pin repositories, packages, templates, and application source before installation, execution, publication, or deployment.
